findings.title: The load-time art warm-up is placed from the camera before the camera first updates, so it is never in the lens and draws nothing
findings.detail: ToonMaterials.warm_up awaits one process_frame and then sets holder.global_position = camera.global_position - camera.global_basis.z * 2.5 + DOWN * 1.2. The process_frame signal fires before the FirstPersonCamera's own _process, so the camera is still at the world origin with an identity basis. The holder lands at (0, -1.2, -2.5), 1.2 m under the floor. Before the first render the camera moves to the eye (y 1.45) and turns to the player's facing (+X in the crowd room). For both frames the holder exists, every corner of the skinned ArtBody's AABB and of the five hull boxes is outside the frustum, so the GPU never draws them and the skinned toon, hull and shadow pipelines are not built at load. SL-int C4 and ARCHITECTURE:992 say it stands 'where the lens sees it'. No windowed test checks this (test_art_punk only checks that it adds nothing headless). The training room uses the same path.

findings.title: A6 misses on the legs (89-91% within hurtbox + 6 cm): the chain never fits girth, so F-punk will repeat it
findings.detail: Hard row A6 needs at least 95% of torso and leg vertices within the hurtbox radius + 6 cm. Every GLB misses on the legs (punk 89.1% of 2,329 vertices, auto 90.9%), and the head sits exactly at the bar (95.0%). The cause is the chain, not only the smoke asset. blender_fit's proportion warp stretches along each bone only and 'never girth' (blender_fit.py:14, P1-chain C3), so whatever thickness Tripo generates ships as is. The same bulk is behind A9's 6.1% cell difference at the jab, A11's 4-5 cm anchor offset and finding 2. In play, a strike that visibly lands on the outer 6 cm or more of the baggy jeans can pass through without a hit, and a contact sinks 4-5 cm into the torso art before the hurtbox registers.

g2.summary:
G2 (deformation and look at 1 m in first person) on m4/art-pipeline @ 59a0adf. The chain does work end to end. The smoke Punk reads as an illustrated character at 1 m, and the palette borders are clean. Two defects, though, are ones the real Punk and the player will both inherit.

(1) The hull's smooth normals are baked in Blender's Z-up axes and are never converted to glTF Y-up. Read back in Godot, the decoded COLOR normal agrees with NORMAL by a mean dot of only 0.338, which is the mean of NORMAL.x² (0.364). Read as Z-up it agrees at 0.930. Every chain GLB has this, the probe body included. As a result the ink line is missing on every top and bottom silhouette: the cap crown, the elbow and forearm bottoms. I patched the shader locally to read the colour as Z-up, recorded once and reverted. That restores a continuous line.

(2) Linear-blend skinning stretches the vest into a fin that rises to the nose during the jab wind-up's hold, and folds the collar and neck in the hook stagger. 122-124 edges grow by more than 2 cm. It looks the same on all four GLBs, so neither weight source nor either bind route fixes it, and the chain's weight smoothing (rig.smooth_iterations) has never been turned on.

Other findings:
- The gloves read as canisters. The glove swatch is 10 luma above ink, the fist is a full mitt where the concept has a fingerless glove, and the cuff flares to 0.083 m.
- Lighting: look_band_2 is 0.62, above cos(52°) = 0.616 for the sun's elevation, so no vertical surface can reach the lit band. In the 1 m acts the Punk's front sits in the violet-tinted shadow band: one band, the teal vest reads blue and the skin reads lilac. Turning the grade off changes neither.
- A7's triangle bar cannot pass on this mesh. 142-177 triangles are flagged in a rigid pose, and 159 are folded in the authored mesh. Without that baseline, the elbow, knee and spine twist pass; the guard is near the bar and the arm raise fails.
- The interior detail is gone (mouth, pockets, stitching), so A18's detail mask is warranted.
- The damage looks turn the skin grey.
- The rim's edge is stippled.

Locks: Tripo weights, the A-pose route, the current fit, border-protected decimation, outline 3.75 px (after the axis fix), 4x MSAA by look (FXAA acceptable), placeholder hulls on.

Verdict: b. The contingency is weight smoothing at named joints, plus A18's mask. The hull-normal axis fix must land first.

votes.reason: The cited stippled patch (C2 f109, left forearm, crop 540,500) is not the rim. The stipple is real, but it is the mid-to-shadow band edge dithered by the shadow map's soft filter, so the finding's cause and its fwidth-rim fix are wrong. In frames I rendered losslessly, the rim never shows on the left forearm, and where the rim does show (the right forearm) its edge is 1-4 px and polygon-crisp.
votes.evidence:
I re-rendered C2 f109 losslessly (PNG sequence, 1600x900, in a scratch copy of the reviewer's worktree at 59a0adf, run by `godot --write-movie`). The unmodified copy was byte-identical to the SL-int frame.

1. The stipple is not JPEG. It shows in the lossless frame as pixel-to-pixel noise (G: 187 192 195 190 197 195 188 184 186 169 188 180 162 165 ...).
2. The patch is not the rim.
   - With `--tune=look_rim_strength=0`, 7,906 pixels change, none in the 100 px cell (600,500) that holds the patch. They are on the right forearm, torso, head and jacket.
   - The patch stat (cream pixels 813, intermediate 971, noise/px 13.0) is unchanged.
   - Diffing against that run shows the rim only as thin strips and one polygon on the right side of the frame. The rim is zero on the left forearm.
   - `look_spec_strength=0` and `look_band_2=1` also leave the patch unchanged.
3. The patch is not albedo. Albedo-only output (DIFFUSE_LIGHT constant) gives a flat tan forearm.
4. It is the shadow-band to mid-band edge, noised by the shadow term.
   - The forearm is in the violet-tinted shadow band and the patch is the mid band.
   - With `lit = ndl` (ATTENUATION dropped), the edge becomes one crisp polygon edge (noise/px 4.29, cream 3,272).
   - With `rendering/lights_and_shadows/directional_shadow/soft_shadow_filter_quality=0` (hard), the stipple also disappears. The patch stays a crisp shadow-terminated shape (noise/px 4.61).
5. The rim is not soft where it actually shows. On the right forearm, the rim's own contribution (base minus rim-off, G channel) rises within 1-4 px:
   - row 560: 2 to 25 in 1 px;
   - row 640: 0, 2, 12, 20, 25;
   - row 700: 2, 21, 29, 34, 39.
   The rim is wider than that only where a flat grazing surface makes it a wide strip, and its edge there is still not stippled.
6. The constants 0.02, 0.3, -0.35 and 0.1 are real literals in the shader. They are shape constants of a smoothstep, not tuning feel numbers. The plan lists only `look_rim_*` (cut, power, strength), and no rubric or measured row (A1-A14, L1-L5, J5) requires a rim-softness tunable. Nothing in the evidence shows the fixed width causing a visible defect.
votes.root_cause:
The rim is smoothstep(rim_cut ± 0.02, pow(1 - N·V, rim_power)) at game/fx/toon_light.gdshaderinc:66-67. On a smooth surface its edge is 1-4 px, and no frame in C2 shows it stippled; the left forearm has no rim at all at f109.

The stipple the finding saw is the shadow-band to mid-band edge. At game/fx/toon_light.gdshaderinc:56, `float lit = ndl * ATTENUATION` puts the sun's shadow-map term inside the band input. Where the Punk's arm is in penumbra at the band_1 (0.25) crossing, Godot's default soft shadow filter makes ATTENUATION a per-pixel dither. That dither gives lit pixel-scale noise around band_1, and the fwidth edge, capped at 0.08, cannot smooth it.

That is a separate low-severity defect in the band logic. Its edge is about 5-8 px and noisy, against the bible's at-most-2-px band edge. It can reappear wherever a self-shadow penumbra crosses a band threshold. An fwidth-based rim would not touch it.

If the lead wants the real defect filed separately, the fix is in the band's shadow handling. Options: take ATTENUATION through its own hard or steep step before multiplying with ndl, or set the directional shadow soft filter to hard or its quality to the lowest. The project does not set it today, so it uses Godot's default.
files_to_change: game/fx/toon_light.gdshaderinc (only for the separate band-edge defect: line 56, `lit = ndl * ATTENUATION`; none for the finding as stated, since the rim is not the cause)
project.godot (alternative for the separate defect: rendering/lights_and_shadows/directional_shadow/soft_shadow_filter_quality; not set today, so the default applies)
